newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude diffs mixed late, sours vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude diffs mixed late, sours vulnerable.

text.p: U.S. crude differentials were mixed in thin trade dampened by volatility in outright prices but light crudes steadied as imports remained scarce.
Heavy, sour barrels appeared more vulnerable to seasonal falls in demand as well as ample regional availabilities.
November West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $24.80-90 a barrel, 80 cents stronger than Wednesday, buoyed by deficits in heating oil and bullish technicals.
But traders said volumes would be thinned by the rally in crude values, as potential buyers take to the sides, and also because of a number of industry functions this week.
The Nov/Dec WTI spread widened out to 60 cents from low 50-cents, helping to revive WTI/Cushing Posting Plus.
The grade traded initially at postings plus $2.30 a barrel, and then $2.32, aided by the firmer spread.
Stronger front-end crude values, underpinned by concerns of cooler temperatures in the U.S. northeast are expected to lead crude prices at Cushing, Oklahoma, traders said.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St James traded within the previous day's range at plus 38/39 cents, while WTI/Midland was also unchanged at WTI plus five cents.
Heavy, sour crudes pared losses but remained weaker.
West Texas Sour/Midland, was reportedly traded at WTI minus $1.37 a barrel, and then recouped to $1.35/1.33.
The market for heavy crudes was seen weighed by upcoming sales of Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) crude and increased supplies from Latin America.
Oriente was seen offered into the U.S. Gulf, along with South Blend and Vasconia.
